definition: Coordinated network of independent, bounded, versioned contexts. Context states, not agents, are the fundamental units.

contexts.title: SCS charter and operating boundary
contexts.purpose: Define the swarm as a context-state coordination protocol; mature its state/data/workflow rules before choosing or building production runtime infrastructure.
contexts.change_note: Version 2 makes repository-native maturation canonical and defers backend/runtime implementation.

contexts.title: Input and task consumption protocol
contexts.purpose: Specify and test how information enters, is normalized, related, prioritized, processed, verified, and recorded.
open_questions: Define and test complete context/task lifecycle transitions; current callable router returns intake decisions but does not itself persist changes.
Decide whether the future context envelope and repository-native context-state schemas can share a stable core.
contexts.change_note: Version 2 adds deterministic intake disposition logic and seven replayable behavior scenarios. CI passes for the named commit.

contexts.title: Repository engineering swarm demonstrator
contexts.purpose: Use the repository's real source files, Git history, metadata, specs, and tests to exercise context-state workflows without a backend.
open_questions: Review legacy/runtime reference artifacts against current context-state contracts.
Populate commit-history and artifact-dependency observations with precise source pointers.
Test context/task state transitions, stale dependency propagation, and conflict reconciliation.
contexts.change_note: Version 2 records an artifact inventory, architecture alignment findings, current GitHub repository observations, and verified CI evidence.

contexts.title: Production backend selection
contexts.purpose: Keep backend choice out of scope until repository-native swarm behavior and implementation contracts have matured.
open_questions: Reopen only after implementation-readiness criteria have evidence and production operational requirements are defined.
contexts.change_note: Version 2 explicitly records that no backend selection, project provisioning, or deployment is part of the current phase.

contexts.title: Observed GitHub state for Context-swarm
contexts.purpose: Preserve source-backed metadata about the repository's visibility, default branch, branch protection, issue listing, commit history, and CI run.
open_questions: Periodically refresh these observations and distinguish current live facts from historical observations.
contexts.change_note: Initial evidence context; recorded facts are scoped to observation date and source response.

work_items.title: Audit existing repository artifacts against the repository-native operating model

priority.rationale: Detect contradictory or premature artifacts before extending the protocol.

acceptance_criteria: Every artifact in the reviewed tree is classified.
Contradictions are recorded with paths and a disposition.
No files are silently deleted.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted: inventory classifies current, deferred, reference-only, and alignment-needed artifacts; four findings record disposition and follow-up.

work_items.title: Add replayable intake and context-state transition cases

priority.rationale: Turn intake rules into observable behavior before implementing a runtime.

acceptance_criteria: Duplicate inputs have deterministic dispositions.
Contradictory claims create a conflict outcome.
Inaccessible sources result in blocked/limited outcomes.
Untrusted embedded instructions remain data.
Consequential actions lacking authorization are blocked.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted for the bounded intake-routing scope. CI run 38954032510 passed. Full persistence and context-state transitions remain separate open work.

work_items.title: Populate the repository engineering context with evidence-backed inventory

priority.rationale: Use actual repository artifacts and connected GitHub source data, not synthetic examples alone.

acceptance_criteria: Repository tree and reviewed commit are recorded.
Artifacts are classified with paths and blob identities where verified.
Known limitations and unresolved questions are recorded.
Claims link to source paths or API evidence.
work_items.last_outcome: Accepted: repository inventory includes reviewed tree, artifact roles, source-backed metadata, CI evidence, and explicit limitations.

work_items.title: Define and test context and task state transitions beyond intake routing

priority.rationale: The router resolves input disposition, but the swarm also needs tested rules for proposing, validating, accepting, blocking, superseding, and versioning context/task state.

acceptance_criteria: Every allowed task transition has preconditions and expected side effects.
Every allowed context transition has preconditions and expected side effects.
Illegal transitions fail closed.
A proposal cannot be confused with accepted state.
Tests cover accepted, blocked, conflicted, stale, and superseded outcomes.

work_items.title: Resolve the relationship between current context-state schema and deferred runtime envelope

priority.rationale: Avoid two incompatible canonical models while preserving a separate future runtime contract until evidence supports consolidation.

acceptance_criteria: List field-level overlap and semantic differences.
Select the canonical repository-native state schema for current phase.
Document which runtime-only fields remain deferred.
Add schema consistency tests without introducing a database.

work_items.title: Expand repository observations with recent commit details and artifact dependency links

priority.rationale: Make the first swarm data set more useful for real repository maintenance and context impact analysis.

acceptance_criteria: Relevant recent commits are summarized with exact commit links.
Artifact dependencies are linked to source paths and tests.
Observed facts are separated from inferences.
Each observation records its date and limitations.

change_note: Registry version 2 records repository-native phase correction, completed inventory/intake tasks, current GitHub evidence, and the next state-machine/schema/evidence tasks.
